# Installation

tidysdmx requires **Python 3.11.9 or later**.

## With pip

```bash
pip install tidysdmx
```

## With uv

```bash
uv add tidysdmx
```

## With Poetry

```bash
poetry add tidysdmx
```

## Optional extras

Signing in to an FMR with Azure (Entra ID) through `AzureTokenProvider.from_default_credential` needs the `azure` extra:

```bash
pip install "tidysdmx[azure]"
```

The core package never imports the Azure SDK, so you can also pass any `azure-identity` credential you build yourself without the extra installed.

## From source (development)

tidysdmx is developed with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/WB-DECIS/tidysdmx.git
cd tidysdmx
make install          # uv sync --all-groups --all-extras, plus the pre-commit hooks
make check            # lint, typecheck, and unit tests with the coverage gate
```

The git hooks run every tool out of the project environment with `uv run`, so
`uv` must be on your `PATH`. `CONTRIBUTING.md` has the details.

## Runtime dependencies

tidysdmx depends on:

- [`pysdmx`](https://py.sdmx.io) — the underlying SDMX information-model library.
- [`httpx`](https://www.python-httpx.org) — pysdmx's HTTP layer, which the FMR client extends so reads and uploads carry a bearer token.
- [`pandas`](https://pandas.pydata.org) — the tabular workhorse.
- [`numpy`](https://numpy.org) — vectorised lookups behind the mapping helpers.
- [`typeguard`](https://typeguard.readthedocs.io) — runtime type checking.
- [`openpyxl`](https://openpyxl.readthedocs.io) — Excel mapping template support.

## Verify the install

```python
import tidysdmx
print(tidysdmx.__version__)

from tidysdmx import (
    create_schema_from_table,
    parse_mapping_template_wb,
    build_structure_map_from_template_wb,
    map_structures,
    standardize_output,
    validate_dataset_local,
)
```

If the imports succeed, you're ready to go. Continue to the [quick start](02-quick-start.qmd).

## Optional: connect to FMR

Most real-world workflows fetch a dissemination schema from a Fusion Metadata Registry. `FmrClient` wraps pysdmx's registry clients and takes care of authentication when the registry needs it:

```python
from tidysdmx import FmrClient

client = FmrClient("https://fmrqa.worldbank.org/FMR")
schema = client.get_schema("WB:IFPRI_ASTI(1.0)", "datastructure")
```

See the [FMR client](03-fmr-client.qmd) chapter for signing in with Azure and uploading artefacts.
